resources.string: Ovary cutaway
Longitudinal section of one adult ovary. The nearby uterine tube is shown for orientation. Scale bar: about 1 cm.
Ovarian cortex
The outer region of the ovary, just under its thin connective tissue capsule, contains follicles at different stages.
Growing follicle
In this small cortical follicle, supporting cells surround the oocyte. A large fluid cavity has not yet formed.
Antral follicle
Fluid fills the antrum of this larger follicle. The oocyte sits off center in a mound of supporting cells against the follicle wall.
Ovarian medulla
The inner connective tissue contains branching blood vessels, lymphatic vessels, and nerves.
Ovarian hilum
Blood vessels and nerves pass between the mesovarium and the medulla at the attached edge of the ovary.
Testis cutaway
Longitudinal section of one adult testis, with its posterior border on the right. Scale bar: about 1 cm.
Tunica albuginea
A dense, pale connective tissue capsule surrounds the testis and thickens at its posterior border to form the mediastinum.
Testicular septum
Thin partitions extend inward from the capsule toward the mediastinum, dividing the interior into lobules. Only a few lobules are shown.
Seminiferous tubules
These tightly coiled tubes lie within the lobules. Near the mediastinum, short straight tubules connect them to the rete testis.
Rete testis
This network lies within the posterior mediastinum. Efferent ductules leave its upper end and enter the head of the epididymis.
Tube cutaway
One uterine tube opened along its length, from the ovary side at left to the uterine corner at right. The inset enlarges a cross section through the ampulla.
Fimbriae
These fingerlike extensions fringe the opening of the tube. They lie near the ovary without sealing the space between the tube and the ovary.
Infundibulum
The flared outer end of the tube opens into the peritoneal cavity beside the ovary.
Ampulla
The long, wide segment between the infundibulum and the isthmus has especially elaborate mucosal folds.
Isthmus
This narrow segment joins the wider ampulla to the short portion that passes through the uterine wall and opens into the uterine cavity.
Mucosal folds
Branching ridges of the lining project into the ampullary lumen. A ring of smooth muscle surrounds the folded mucosa.
Lining layers
Magnified cutaway of the uterine lining in the proliferative phase, with the uterine cavity above. Lining thickness varies over the cycle.
Surface epithelium
A single layer of columnar cells faces the uterine cavity and continues into the openings of the uterine glands.
Functional layer
The portion nearest the cavity contains stroma, glands, and spiral arterioles. It grows during the cycle and is shed at menstruation.
Uterine gland
The tubular glands open onto the surface and extend through the functional layer into the basal layer. They are relatively straight in the proliferative phase.
Basal layer
This deep portion of the endometrium lies against the myometrium. It remains after menstruation and gives rise to the next functional layer.
Myometrium
Interlacing smooth muscle bundles form the thick uterine wall under the endometrium. Only a shallow part is shown here.
